To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) stationary-phase cultures of uropathogenic Esch. coli are phenotypically heterogeneous and (ii) this heterogeneity enables bacteria to escape serum complement killing and antibiotic action.

(i) the complement component C3 binds to the surface of UPEC strain Cft073 cells and that (ii) the heterogeneity of cell division in stationary-phase cells enables three different subpopulations of CFT073 to be distinguished, with the rapidly growing cells resisting serum complement-mediated lyses, the cells with intermediate growth rates being sensitive to complement, and the non-growing population resisting both serum and antibiotics.
the heterogeneity of UPEC cells in the stationary phase of growth is a prerequisite to their resistance to killing by the complement system and antibiotics.

the ability of UPEC to survive serum complement and antibiotic treatment.
